title: Token Tide Regulator and Attention Prefetch Smoother
creator: Aisha Mendez
description:
Summary: We observe recurring tail-latency spikes for mixed-length workloads where short requests (1–50 tokens) interleave with long prefill-heavy requests. Root causes appear to be (1) premature batch closure that forces small kernel invocations and prevents coalescing, (2) attention-prefetch scheduling that doesn't prioritize kernels that benefit most from KV reuse, and (3) admission logic that treats heterogeneous token-costs uniformly.

Goal: Implement the 'Token Tide Regulator' (TTR) + Attention Prefetch Smoother to reduce 95/99 p95/p99 latency for mixed workloads by improving admission pacing and prefill-to-decode handoff. Target metrics: p95 reduced by >=15% and p99 reduced by >=20% on the mixed benchmark suite without >5% tail regression on pure short-request traffic.

Proposed design:
- Token Tide Regulator (admission windowing): maintain a sliding token-budget window per GPU pool that measures tokens-in-flight (token-seconds) instead of request-count. New requests are admitted if there is headroom; otherwise they are queued for the next micro-window. This biases admission toward high-throughput-friendly sequences and prevents micro-bursts of tiny requests from starving kernel-coalescing opportunities.

- Graceful close vs eager close: implement adaptive batch finalization where the batch close timer is a function of current token-budget utilization and kernel affinity hints. If expected remaining decode tokens in the batch are >X, extend the close window slightly to allow additional compatible short requests that increase kernel efficiency.

- Attention Prefetch Smoother: when prefill requests arrive, compute an attention-priority score (based on sequence length, model-arch features, and KV-hit-rate heuristics). Prefetch scheduling will re-order prefill tasks within the admission buffer to prioritize those that enable KV cache reuse and avoid scattering attention-heavy kernels across time.

- Kernel hinting and soft-fallbacks: admission now attaches a kernel-hint based on sequence length quantiles; the scheduler tries to assemble batches that maximize a single kernel path. If full alignment is impossible, TTR allows one speculative slot for a best-effort coalescing attempt and records telemetry for future tuning.

- Metrics and safety knobs: expose the token-window size, grace multiplier, speculative-slot fraction, and attention-priority weights as runtime knobs. Add canary flags to apply the policy per-tenant or per-route.

Acceptance criteria:
- Internal bench: p95 decreased by >=15% and p99 decreased by >=20% on mixed workloads compared to baseline continuous-batcher for the same throughput.
- No more than 5% increase in average latency for pure short-request workloads.
- Telemetry: per-kernel utilization increases by >=10% for kernels handling long-prefill workloads.
- Graceful rollback path and per-route opt-out toggles implemented.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Need careful synchronization with KV cache lifetimes; ensure admission scheduler propagates expected KV footprint to the cache manager to avoid eviction storms.
- Kernel-hinting requires a small metadata addition to the admission header (2 bytes). Backward compatibility: defaults to 'no-hint' if older nodes present.
- Expect slight increase in scheduler CPU; measure and gate with cpu-threshold knob.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit tests + simulator for admission behavior (short/long mixes, bursts). (ENGs: Rohan, Ying)
2) Internal canary on 10% of hosted traffic with the token-window conservative defaults. Collect 72h telemetry.
3) Expand to 50% with telemetry review; enable per-route opt-in for lower-latency customers.
4) Full rollout once p99 and kernel-util targets met.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: over-aggressive coalescing could increase tail for very low-latency SLAs. Mitigation: per-tenant opt-out, and default conservative window sizes.
- Risk: interaction with autoscaling (burst admission may make GPUs appear saturated). Mitigation: surface token-window utilization to autoscaler and provide a smoothing signal.
- Risk: incorrect KV lifetime hints could increase cache churn. Mitigation: start with passive-mode where hints only inform scheduling without prompting evictions.

Notes: design inspired by capacity-window research tickets but avoids granular kernel-reweighting complexity in first pass. This ticket focuses on pragmatic admission pacing + attention-aware prefetch ordering.
